Topic.label: Linear Functions and Linear Equations in One Variable

Question: The x-coordinate of the intersection of the graph of the linear function \(y=kx+b\) with the x-axis equals the solution of the equation \(kx+b=0\). Given that the solution of this equation is \(x=3\) and the graph passes through \((0,-6)\), find the value of \(k\).
Solution: The solution of the equation is 3, indicating that the graph passes through \((3,0)\). It also passes through \((0,-6)\), so \(b=-6\), \(3k-6=0\), and \(k=2\).
